Delete and undelete sets, and show or change their retention

```sh
goback [global flags] set <command>
```

## set delete

Close a set and retire its commits; --erase skips the trash window

```sh
goback [global flags] set delete [flags] <name>
```

| Flag | Description | Environment | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--erase` | tombstone the commits at once instead of after the trash window |  |  |

## set undelete

Reopen a set before its commits are tombstoned

```sh
goback [global flags] set undelete <name>
```

## set retention

Show or change the retention of a set, or the store's defaults without a name; a keep flag replaces the policy, --inherit drops it

```sh
goback [global flags] set retention [flags] [<name>]
```

| Flag | Description | Environment | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--keep-last value` | keep the newest this many commits |  |  |
| `--keep value` | a bracket as &lt;period&gt;=&lt;count&gt; calendar periods, newest first, repeated; the last may drop its count to keep forever (--keep hourly=336 --keep daily=60 --keep weekly=12 --keep monthly) |  |  |
| `--keep-within value` | keep every commit younger than this |  |  |
| `--inherit` | drop the policy: a set inherits the store's, the store uses the built-in |  |  |
| `--trash-days value` | store only: days a deleted commit waits for its tombstone |  | `-1` |
